title: U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Top 5,400
excerpt: The U.S. has lost the measles elimination status it held since 2000, after a panel found the virus has spread continuously for over a year. CDC: 5,412 cases in 2026.
content:
The United States has lost the measles elimination status it held since 2000, after an independent panel of experts found the virus has spread continuously inside the country for more than a year, according to reports first published Friday, November 13.

The decision was reported by The Wall Street Journal and confirmed to CNN by a source close to the process. An independent commission of experts reporting to the director of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional office for the Americas, reviewed epidemiological and laboratory evidence submitted by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Neither PAHO nor the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services had officially confirmed the decision when the reports were published, and a formal announcement is expected on Tuesday, November 17, according to NBC News and CIDRAP.

What elimination status means

Elimination status is a formal designation, not a claim that a country has zero cases. A country loses it when the same strain of measles is passed from person to person without interruption for at least 12 months, the threshold for endemic transmission. The United States was certified as having eliminated measles in 2000.

The evidence pointing to that threshold included a study from scientists at Utah’s public health laboratory, published as a preprint in August, showing the same strain of measles had circulated in the state for more than a year, accounting for more than 95 percent of cases there.

To win the status back, the United States will now need to go 12 months without continuous transmission.

The 2026 numbers

The CDC’s weekly update on November 13 put the 2026 case total at 5,412 across 45 states and Washington, D.C., up 230 in a week and the 14th straight week of a triple-digit increase, according to CIDRAP. That is the highest annual total since 1991, and far above the 2,289 cases recorded in all of 2025.

People have been hospitalized in roughly 1 in 9 reported cases this year, according to the CDC. State health departments now report 10 measles-associated deaths in 2026; the CDC’s own count stood at six deaths after its latest update. Canada is the only other country in the Americas region that has already lost its elimination status.

A Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson said the mission does not change whatever PAHO determines, and that HHS and the CDC will continue working to stop transmission, close vaccination gaps, and strengthen outbreak response. Secretary Kennedy and CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.

What it means for Webb County

Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known, and it spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Health experts point to falling childhood vaccination rates as the main driver of the virus’s return. The CDC’s guidance is that the MMR vaccine is the most effective protection against measles. Readers with questions about their own or their children’s vaccination status should contact their health care provider or the Webb County public health office. Webb Watch 956 will keep reporting the official case counts and the formal PAHO announcement when it is published.
